DK92.0 is a medical diagnosis code representing hematemesis (vomiting blood) [^src1]. In the context of the Danish healthcare system's quality monitoring, it is utilized as part of a broader set of diagnostic codes to track the incidence of severe bleeding among patients with [[atrieflimren]] [^src1]. Specifically, DK92.0 falls under the category of gastrointestinal bleeding codes, alongside others like [[dk25-0|DK25.0]] through [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]], [[dk92-1|DK92.1]], and [[dk92-2|DK92.2]] [^src1]. 

The code is formally integrated into the clinical quality indicators for the national Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK), managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute [^src2] [^src3]. When measuring the incidence of [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] (severe bleeding), healthcare registries use DK92.0 in combination with codes for intracranial bleeding (e.g., [[di60|DI60]]–[[ds066|DS066]]) and urinary/respiratory tract bleeding (e.g., [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], [[dr31|DR31]]) to ensure comprehensive capture of adverse bleeding events in this patient population [^src1]. The consistent inclusion of DK92.0 in the annual AFDK methodology reports from 2023 through 2025 underscores its stable role in defining gastrointestinal bleeding complications for cardiovascular quality assurance [^src1] [^src2] [^src3].
